blocks.passage:
Negotiation across cultures is different from negotiation at home. What sounds direct in one country may sound rude in another. What sounds polite in one may sound weak in another.

The safe rule: stay polite and clear. Use soft language — Could we, Would you, Is it possible. Ask questions before you make demands. Give time to think.

Most international deals are not won by the loudest voice. They are won by the side that listens well and keeps its promises.

items.q: How is negotiation across cultures different from at home?
options: What sounds direct or polite in one country may sound rude or weak in another
items.why: "What sounds direct in one country may sound rude in another."

items.q: What is the safe rule?
items.why: "The safe rule: stay polite and clear."

items.q: Which is an example of 'soft language'?
items.why: "Use soft language — Could we, Would you, Is it possible."

items.q: What should you do before making demands?
items.why: "Ask questions before you make demands."

items.q: Who wins most international deals?
options: The side with the biggest ship
The side that listens well and keeps its promises
items.why: "They are won by the side that listens well and keeps its promises."

audio.text:
It's your first call with our new distributor in India, so before you dial, let me give you a few simple tips. Nothing complicated — just polite and patient.

First, soft language. Don't say 'I need this by Friday'. Say 'Would it be possible to have this by Friday?' Same request, but it sounds respectful, not like an order. Use 'Could we', 'Would you', 'Is it possible'. It opens doors.

Second, ask before you tell. Start by asking about their business, their needs, their timeline. When you understand them first, your own points land much better.

Third, give time to think. Don't rush them to say yes on the call. In many cultures, a quick yes under pressure isn't a real yes. Let them consider it and come back.

And fourth, whatever you agree, keep your promise. If you say you'll send something on Monday, send it on Monday. Reliability builds trust faster than any clever words.

Polite, patient, and reliable. Do that, and the relationship starts well.

items.q: Who is the call with?
items.why: "your first call with our new distributor in India."

items.q: What is the first tip?
options: Use soft language — 'Would it be possible…' instead of 'I need…'
items.why: "Don't say 'I need this by Friday'. Say 'Would it be possible…'"

items.q: What does 'ask before you tell' mean?
options: Ask about their business and needs before making your points
items.why: "Start by asking about their business, their needs, their timeline."

items.q: Why give time to think?
options: In many cultures, a quick yes under pressure isn't a real yes
items.why: "a quick yes under pressure isn't a real yes."

items.q: What builds trust faster than clever words?
items.why: "Reliability builds trust faster than any clever words."

items.q: **Soft language** is…
items.why: Soft language = linguagem suave.

items.q: A **demand** is…
items.why: Demand = exigência.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Being **___** means saying please and thank you and respecting the other side."
items.why: Polite = educado.

items.q: A **compromise** is…
options: a total win for one side
an agreement where each side gives a little
items.why: Compromise = concessão, meio-termo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Being **___** means you can wait calmly for a decision."
items.why: Patient = paciente.

items.q: "Soft language **opens doors**." To open doors means to…
items.why: Open doors = abrir portas.

items.q: "Don't **rush them** to say yes." To rush someone means to…
items.why: Rush = apressar.

items.q: "When you understand them first, your points **land** better." To land here means to…
items.why: Land = ser bem recebido, surtir efeito.

items.q: "Always **keep your promise**." To keep a promise means to…
options: do what you said you would
items.why: Keep your promise = cumprir a promessa.

items.q: "Reliability **builds trust**." To build trust means to…
items.why: Build trust = construir confiança.
